supplement.where: Appendices A–G included in the thesis PDF.
supplement.holds: Recruitment poster, consent form, training slides, trust and demographics questionnaires, research ethics protocol, and interview codes with sample quotes. No additional sketch-outcome inferential statistics or assignment-sequence mechanism are provided in these appendices.

paper_design_summary: A laboratory study recruited 26 adults around Carleton University to sketch websites using Gemini-generated inspiration, Google search inspiration, and no external inspiration. Every participant experienced all three conditions, with fully counterbalanced condition order and varying task-condition combinations, but random assignment of sequences is not stated (PDF p. 27, printed p. 19, §3.1; PDF p. 30, printed p. 22, §3.4.1). Final sketches were scored for originality using expert clustering and for design fixation using the proportion of features copied from each participant’s inspiration samples (PDF pp. 33–35 and 40, printed pp. 25–27 and 32, §3.4.2).

assignment.what_was_assigned: Source of inspiration: AI (Gemini), Search Engine (Google), or No Inspiration. Each participant experienced all three conditions. Condition order was fully counterbalanced and website-task/condition combinations varied across participants; the mechanism for assigning participants to sequences was not stated.
assignment.quote: We adopted a within-subjects design, with participants exposed to each of the three experiment conditions. The order of the conditions was fully counterbalanced across participants.

arms.name: AI
arms.description: Within-person condition with access to Gemini for participant-generated design inspiration. Part of the shared study sample; per-condition analyzed count is not explicitly reported. PDF pp. 30–31 (printed pp. 22–23), §3.4.1.

arms.name: Search Engine
arms.description: Within-person condition with Google search in Microsoft Edge for design inspiration. Part of the shared study sample; per-condition analyzed count is not explicitly reported. PDF pp. 30–31 (printed pp. 22–23), §3.4.1.

arms.name: No Inspiration
arms.description: Within-person control condition relying on participants’ own knowledge and experience, without external design support. Part of the shared study sample; per-condition analyzed count is not explicitly reported. PDF pp. 30–31 (printed pp. 22–23), §3.4.1.

participants.who: Adults recruited through posters around Carleton University; prior design experience was not required. The paper reports 26 recruited people but does not explicitly state the analyzed count for the sketch outcomes. Student status is not established for the whole sample. The recruited count is retained here rather than substituted for an analyzed count.
participants.quote: Twenty-six participants were recruited for this study.
participants.locator: PDF p. 27 (printed p. 19), §3.1 Participants; PDF p. 45 (printed p. 37), §3.5 Experiment Procedure; PDF pp. 46–47 (printed pp. 38–39), §§4.1.1–4.1.2 report sketch outcomes without explicit analysis counts.

ai_tool.how_used: Participants could prompt Gemini as often as they wanted during sketching to generate their own design inspiration. Training demonstrated how to request an image of a website interface. PDF pp. 30–31 (printed pp. 22–23), §3.4.1.

task.description: Create a final paper sketch of a new website for each of a mall, an educational institution, and a travel booking company, with features labelled. Task-condition combinations varied between participants; only final sketches were analyzed. PDF pp. 29–30 (printed pp. 21–22), §3.3 and Table 3.2.
task.duration: No task time limit; full session approximately 60 minutes. PDF p. 30 (printed p. 22), §3.3; PDF p. 45 (printed p. 37), §3.5.

outcomes.name: Originality of final sketches (per-sketch rarity from expert clustering)
outcomes.question: with_ai

contrasts.reported: AI M = 80.32% (SD = 11.37%); Search Engine M = 81.50% (SD = 10.26%); No Inspiration M = 83.13% (SD = 9.04%). Omnibus Friedman test across all three conditions: χ²(2) = 0.804, W = 0.015, p = 0.669; no significant differences. A pairwise AI-versus-comparator test is not reported.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 46 (printed p. 38), §4.1.1 Originality; scoring method: PDF pp. 33–34 (printed pp. 25–26), §3.4.2 Originality.

outcomes.name: Design fixation (proportion of final-sketch features copied from viewed inspiration)
outcomes.question: with_ai

contrasts.reported: AI M = 52.85% (SD = 31.64%) versus Search Engine M = 23.98% (SD = 22.57%). Wilcoxon signed-ranks test: Z = -3.19, p = 0.001; significantly higher design fixation with AI. This measures copying from each participant’s inspiration samples, not similarity between different participants’ outputs.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 47 (printed p. 39), §4.1.2 Design Fixation and Figure 4.1; scoring method: PDF pp. 35 and 40 (printed pp. 27 and 32), §3.4.2 Measuring Design Fixation.

eligibility.reason: The reported recruited sample is 26 people, so the study cannot meet the minimum of 50 analyzed people; the exact analyzed count is not explicitly reported (PDF p. 27, printed p. 19, §3.1; PDF pp. 46–47, printed pp. 38–39, §§4.1.1–4.1.2). All participants experienced all conditions in a fully counterbalanced order, but the text does not state random assignment of condition order or how sequences were allocated (PDF p. 30, printed p. 22, §3.4.1). Counterbalancing alone does not establish either random or non-random allocation, so criterion 1 remains unclear and design_class is other. Final-sketch originality is scored by expert clustering, and design fixation is scored from copied features, satisfying criterion 3 (PDF pp. 33–35 and 40, printed pp. 25–27 and 32, §3.4.2). Context class is none because a qualifying observational allocation mechanism is not established; the study is excluded from core on sample size regardless.

one_line_finding: Gemini inspiration produced higher design fixation than search (M = 52.85% versus 23.98%; p = 0.001), while originality did not differ significantly across AI, search, and no-inspiration conditions (omnibus Friedman p = 0.669; PDF pp. 46–47, printed pp. 38–39, §§4.1.1–4.1.2).
